read.sections.0.heading.back: A sense of belonging is more than just being present
read.sections.0.heading.source: Belonging is more than being there

read.sections.0.text.note: Translator: The Ubuntu saying 'a person is a person through other people' is rendered as 'seseorang menjadi manusia melalui orang lain'. Check that it sounds natural and true to the saying. Back-translation check: Ubuntu saying rendered as 'seseorang menjadi manusia melalui orang lain'. Check that it sounds natural and stays true to the saying.
read.sections.0.text.back: A sense of belonging is the feeling of being accepted by and close to a group. A person can sit in a room together with a group but still feel ignored or left out. People can be part of many kinds of groups at the same time, such as a class, a sports team, a group of friends or a club. The group might also be people who share a language or a hobby. Many cultures value connections like this. In southern Africa, people often talk about Ubuntu. Ubuntu is usually explained as “a person becomes human through other people”. This means that we grow as human beings through our relationships with other people.
read.sections.0.text.source: Belonging is the feeling of being accepted and connected to a group. A person can sit in a room with a group and still feel ignored or left out. People can belong to many kinds of groups at once, such as a class, a sports team, a group of friends or a club. It might also be people who share a language or a hobby. Many cultures value these connections. In southern Africa, people often talk about Ubuntu. It is usually explained as “a person is a person through other people”. It means we grow as people through our relationships with others.

read.sections.0.simpler.back: A sense of belonging means you feel accepted in a group. You feel close to the people in that group. A person can be in a room but still feel left out. People can be members of many groups. For example a class, a team or friends. It can also people who share a language or a hobby. In southern Africa, people talk about Ubuntu. It means we grow as human beings through other people.
read.sections.0.simpler.source: Belonging means you feel accepted in a group. You feel connected to the people in it. A person can be in a room and still feel left out. People can belong to many groups. It can be a class, a team or friends. It can be people who share a language or a hobby. In southern Africa, people talk about Ubuntu. It means we grow as people through other people.

read.sections.1.text.note: Back-translation check: 'Explained the rules quietly' became 'dengan tenang' (calmly). This is a small shift in meaning. Keep it consistent with whatever is chosen for Card 1.
read.sections.1.text.back: A barrier is something that makes it difficult for a person to take part. Look at those youth club feedback cards. One member feels meetings are difficult when everyone talks at the same time. Another member only joined the club after someone explained the rules calmly. The club does not need to change its members. Instead, the club can change the way it runs. A rule of speaking in turns makes meetings easier to follow, because only one person speaks at a time. A welcoming friend can explain the club's routine to new members. These changes remove barriers, so more people can take part.
read.sections.1.text.source: A barrier is something that makes it harder for someone to take part. Look at the youth club's feedback cards. One member finds meetings difficult when everyone speaks at once. Another member only joined after someone explained the rules quietly. The club does not need to change its members. Instead, it can change how it works. Turn-taking rules make meetings easier to follow, because only one person speaks at a time. A welcome partner can explain the club's routines to new members. These changes remove barriers, so more people can participate.

read.sections.1.simpler.back: Barriers make it difficult for us to take part. Read the cards of that club. One member feels it is difficult when everyone talks at the same time. Another one joined the club after someone explained the rules. The club does not need to change its members. The club can change the way it runs. By speaking in turns, one person speaks at a time. A welcoming friend can explain the club's routine. Now more people can take part.
read.sections.1.simpler.source: A barrier makes it hard to take part. Read the club's cards. One person finds it hard when everyone talks at once. One person joined after someone explained the rules. The club does not need to change its members. It can change how it works. With turn-taking, one person speaks at a time. A welcome partner can explain the routines. Now more people can join in.

read.sections.2.text.note: Translator: 'UN' is rendered as 'PBB' (Pertubuhan Bangsa-Bangsa Bersatu), the usual Malaysian abbreviation. Check whether young readers will know it. Back-translation check: 'PBB' for UN, and 'Perjanjian PBB tentang hak kanak-kanak' is a loose rendering, not the official title ('Konvensyen mengenai Hak Kanak-Kanak'). Check that young readers know 'PBB'.
read.sections.2.text.back: A sense of belonging also grows when people truly get to have a say. One card says: “I want to help choose the activities, not only attend them”. A student planning group gives members more ability to act, that is, the power to make choices and to act. The UN agreement on children's rights states that children have the right to give their opinions about matters that affect them. That agreement also states that they can join or set up groups. A good group asks its members what works and what does not. Nobody needs to share personal things about their life in order to be part of a group.
read.sections.2.text.source: Belonging also grows when people have a real say. One card says: “I want to help choose the activities, not only attend them”. A student planning group gives members more agency, which means the power to make choices and act. The UN agreement on children's rights says children have the right to give their opinions on things that affect them. It also says they can join or set up groups. A good group asks members what is working and what is not. Nobody should have to share private things about their life to belong.

read.sections.2.simpler.note: Back-translation check: Fixed the last sentence: it said 'to feel accepted', but the English says 'to belong'. It now matches the standard text. Check that it still reads simply.
read.sections.2.simpler.back: A sense of belonging grows when people get to have a say. One member wants to help choose what the club does. A planning group gives members more ability to act. They can make choices and act. A UN agreement states children have the right to give their opinions. They can join or set up groups. A good group asks what works and what does not. Nobody needs to share personal things in order to feel accepted.
read.sections.2.simpler.source: Belonging grows when people have a say. One member wants to help choose what the club does. A planning group gives members more agency. They can make choices and act. A UN agreement says children have a right to give their opinions. They can join groups or start them. A good group asks what works and what does not. No one has to share private things to belong.

watch.summary.back: In this video, young people talk about identity, sense of belonging and ability to act at the place where they study. Their identity grows from their experiences. This includes goals they have achieved and mistakes that became lessons for them. A sense of belonging grows when adults know students' names. It also grows when students can share their work without being judged. For them, ability to act means feeling confident that you can achieve goals if you make an effort. Older mentors, friends and opportunities to lead can help. At the end of the video, they tell adults that young people are already ready to help shape their own lives and schools. The speakers in the video share their own stories, but you do not need to share your story. You can think about those questions by using that youth club, or a group that you know.
watch.summary.source: In this video, young people talk about identity, belonging and agency in the places where they learn. Their identity grows from their experiences. These include goals they reached and mistakes they learned from. Belonging grows when adults know students' names. It also grows when students can share their work and not be judged. For them, agency means feeling sure that you can reach a goal if you work at it. Older helpers, friends and chances to lead can help. At the end, they tell adults that young people are ready to help shape their own lives and schools. The speakers share their own stories, but you do not need to share yours. You can think about the questions using the youth club, or a group you know.

sensitiveNotes.0.back: Ask a local educator to check this lesson before it is used. For some students, the topic of sense of belonging can stir up feelings about their place of origin, family or loss.
sensitiveNotes.0.source: Please have a local educator review this lesson before use. Belonging can bring up feelings about home, family or loss for some learners.

sensitiveNotes.1.note: Back-translation check: 'Their own home' became 'tempat tinggal' (where they live). For displaced learners, 'home' may also mean their homeland. Note 0 uses 'tempat asal'. Consider 'rumah atau tempat asal' so both meanings are covered.
sensitiveNotes.1.back: Never ask students to talk about where they live, their family or their own past, or moments when they felt left out. The youth club, classes, teams, friend groups, languages or hobbies are always suitable to use as examples.
sensitiveNotes.1.source: Never ask learners to talk about their own home, family, past or times they did not belong. The youth club, a class, a team, a group of friends, a language or a hobby always work as examples.

sensitiveNotes.2.back: If a student chooses to share something personal, listen calmly, say thank you, and do not ask follow-up questions in front of the group. Follow your centre's protection steps if you are worried.
